question: An investigator is studying gene expression in a mouse model. She inactivates the assembly of small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs) in motor nerve cells. Which of the following processes is most likely to be affected as a result?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Inactivation of snRNPs in motor nerve cells -> Impaired splicing of pre-mRNA -> Accumulation of unprocessed mRNA -> Disrupted protein synthesis -> Impaired folding of proteins -> Affecting the folding of proteins -> 85%

CHAIN: Inactivation of snRNPs in motor nerve cells -> Impaired splicing of pre-mRNA -> Accumulation of unprocessed mRNA -> Disrupted protein synthesis -> Impaired removal of introns -> Affecting the removal of introns -> 80%
enhanced_information: Inactivation of snRNPs in motor nerve cells leads to impaired splicing of pre-mRNA, resulting in the accumulation of unprocessed mRNA. This disrupts protein synthesis, affecting both the folding of proteins and the removal of introns. The most likely process to be affected as a result is the removal of introns.
analysis: Inactivation of snRNPs in motor nerve cells leads to impaired splicing of pre-mRNA, resulting in the accumulation of unprocessed mRNA. This primarily affects the removal of introns, disrupting the normal process of gene expression. While the folding of proteins can be indirectly impacted due to disrupted protein synthesis, the removal of introns is the most likely process to be affected.
